issue.title: [cfggen] len() called with no arguments crashes PortChannel Fallback parsing

failure.body:
### Description

`minigraph.py:969` calls `len()` with no arguments inside the PortChannel Fallback branch, causing a `TypeError` at runtime whenever a PortChannel with a Fallback element is parsed from minigraph.

### Current code
```python
pcs[pcintfname] = {'fallback': pcintf.find(str(QName(ns, "Fallback"))).text,
                   'min_links': str(int(math.ceil(len() * 0.75))),  # <-- len() with NO args
                   'lacp_key': 'auto'}
```

Compare with the correct code 2 lines below which uses `len(pcmbr_list)`.

### Fix
Change `len()` to `len(pcmbr_list)`.

### Impact
Any PortChannel with a `<Fallback>` element in the minigraph XML will crash `sonic-cfggen` with `TypeError: len() takes exactly one argument (0 given)`.

### How to reproduce
Parse a minigraph XML containing a PortChannel with a Fallback element.

resolution.title: [agent][cfggen] Fix len() called with no arguments in PortChannel Fallback parsing
resolution.description:
#### What I did
Fix `len()` called with no arguments in `minigraph.py:969`, which crashes PortChannel Fallback parsing with `TypeError`.

#### How I did it
Changed `len()` to `len(pcmbr_list)`, matching the non-Fallback branch on line 971.

#### How to verify it
Parse a minigraph XML containing a PortChannel with a `<Fallback>` element — it should no longer crash.

#### Which release branch to backport
master

#### Description for the changelog
Fix TypeError crash in minigraph PortChannel Fallback parsing due to len() called with no arguments.

Fixes: #26399
